title: SLO Neighborhood Initiative Journal and Operational Contract
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: individual service-level SLOs are noisy for services with bursty traffic and cross-region fallbacks. Teams are struggling to make prioritization decisions because error budget burn appears unrelated across services that share common infrastructure or routing. Goal: introduce the concept of 'SLO neighborhoods'—logical groupings of services that share SLI characteristics and dependencies—and implement an initiative-level ledger and operational contract for tracking combined error budgets, rollout gates, and on-call handoffs. Scope: create tracking model, UI cards in the Initiative Hub, a phased rollout for 6 pilot neighborhoods, automated combined-sli dashboards, and an operational contract template (runbook + escalation matrix) that product and platform teams sign off on. Out of scope: changing individual SLI definitions or thresholds during pilot; modifying infra routing behavior as an outcome of this ticket (those are follow-on engineering projects).
acceptance_criteria: Definition: SLO neighborhood schema documented and approved by at least 3 platform/product leads
Telemetry: Combined SLI calculation implemented for pilot neighborhoods and visible in the Initiative Hub dashboard
Contract: Operational contract template published in Confluence and used by pilot teams
Gating: Error-budget gating logic implemented (soft alerts + hard gating suggestion) and validated with synthetic tests
Rollout: 6 pilot neighborhoods onboarded, each with owner, on-call handoff, and a documented mitigation playbook
